vocabulary.meaning_en: planning and controlling a piece of work from start to finish
vocabulary.example: She took a course in project management.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a plan to reach a goal
vocabulary.example: We need a clear strategy for Europe.

vocabulary.meaning_en: try to win customers by offering lower prices
vocabulary.example: Small shops can't always compete on price.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a company or person you compete against
vocabulary.example: Our main rival is targeting the same market.

vocabulary.word: price someone out of the market
vocabulary.meaning_en: offer prices so low that competitors cannot sell
vocabulary.example: We need to price our rivals out of the market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: control most of the sales of a product
vocabulary.example: They cornered the market in mobile phones.

vocabulary.meaning_en: develop good connections with people over time
vocabulary.example: We need to build good relationships with our customers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: talk briefly to check how things are going
vocabulary.example: Let's touch base next week about the project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: talk to someone to learn the latest news
vocabulary.example: Let's catch up after the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: sign a contract officially
vocabulary.example: The client hasn't signed on the dotted line yet.

vocabulary.meaning_en: aim a product or service at a group
vocabulary.example: They are targeting the European market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: just manage to survive, especially with money
vocabulary.example: The company is trying to keep its head above water.

vocabulary.meaning_en: responsible for something or someone
vocabulary.example: I've put you in charge of the project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: know nothing about something
vocabulary.example: I don't have a clue how this machine works.

vocabulary.meaning_en: be the strongest or most important
vocabulary.example: The company dominates the market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: how much something is worth for its price
vocabulary.example: Our products are good quality and good value.

vocabulary.meaning_en: meeting in person, not by phone
vocabulary.example: Let's discuss this face to face.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extra money paid for good work
vocabulary.example: Everyone got a bonus at the end of the year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: making people believe something
vocabulary.example: Her plan was very convincing.

vocabulary.meaning_en: charge too much or give poor quality (informal)
vocabulary.example: That shop tried to rip me off.

vocabulary.meaning_en: ask someone to pay too much
vocabulary.example: Please check the bill; I think they overcharged us.

fine_lines.title: rival vs partner
fine_lines.explanation_ar: rival منافس تحاول التغلّب عليه، وpartner شريك تعمل معه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A rival competes against you. A partner works with you.

examples.sentence: We signed a deal with a new partner in Spain.

fine_lines.title: touch base vs catch up
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما للحديث عن المستجدات؛ touch base قصير ورسمي في العمل غالبًا، وcatch up أعمّ ويُستخدم مع الأصدقاء أيضًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean talk about the latest news. Touch base is a short work check-in; catch up is more general, also with friends.

examples.sentence: I'll touch base with you on Monday.

expressions.phrase: We've got to compete on price.
expressions.meaning_ar: يجب أن ننافس من خلال السعر.
expressions.meaning_en: We must win customers with lower prices.
expressions.example: Our rivals are cheaper, so we've got to compete on price.

expressions.phrase: We need to price our rivals out of the market.
expressions.meaning_ar: علينا إخراج منافسينا من السوق بأسعارنا.
expressions.meaning_en: Our prices must be so low that rivals can't sell.
expressions.example: To win, we need to price our rivals out of the market.

expressions.phrase: We need to corner the market.
expressions.meaning_en: We must control most of the sales.
expressions.example: With this new product, we can corner the market.

expressions.phrase: We need to build good relationships with our customers.
expressions.meaning_ar: علينا بناء علاقات جيدة مع عملائنا.
expressions.meaning_en: We must give customers good service and keep in contact.
expressions.example: We need to build good relationships with our customers, so let's call them regularly.

expressions.phrase: We need to touch base about the project.
expressions.meaning_ar: نحتاج إلى التواصل بشأن سير المشروع.
expressions.example: Could you come to my office? We need to touch base about the project.

expressions.phrase: Have they signed on the dotted line yet?
expressions.example: Good news, but have they signed on the dotted line yet?

grammar.title: need to / have got to for strategy and obligation
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم need to + فعل مجرد وhave got to + فعل مجرد للتعبير عمّا هو ضروري في الخطة. We need to... / We've got to...
grammar.explanation_en: Use need to + base verb and have got to + base verb to say what is necessary in a plan.
examples: We need to corner the market.
We've got to compete on price.
We need to talk to our customers regularly.

grammar.title: so that for purpose
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم so that لبيان الهدف: الجملة الأولى + so that + جملة كاملة.
grammar.explanation_en: Use so that to give a purpose: clause + so that + full clause.
examples: We need to corner the market so that everyone knows us.
Call clients often so that they feel valued.
Lower the price so that more people buy.

questions.question: "Touch base" at work means...
questions.explanation_ar: touch base تعني التواصل للاطمئنان على سير العمل.
questions.explanation_en: It means a short talk to check progress.

questions.question: We need to ___ the market (control most of the sales).
questions.explanation_ar: corner the market تعني الاستحواذ على السوق.
questions.explanation_en: Corner the market = control most sales.

questions.question: A company you compete against is a...
"Sign on the dotted line" means...
questions.explanation_en: It means officially sign a contract.

questions.question: "Price our rivals out of the market" means...
choices: make prices so low rivals can't sell
questions.explanation_ar: تعني خفض الأسعار حتى لا يستطيع المنافسون البيع.
questions.explanation_en: Prices so low that rivals cannot sell.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: We need to build good relationships.
We need to building good relationships.
We needs to build good relationships.

questions.question: "Rip someone off" means...
questions.explanation_ar: rip off تعني المبالغة في السعر أو الاحتيال.
questions.explanation_en: Rip off = charge too much or give poor goods.

questions.question: Lower the price ___ more people buy it.
Extra money for good work is a...
questions.explanation_en: A bonus is extra money for good work.
